correctness.rationale: Proved the normalization-circle exact sequence for totally real real-P1 rational components and the real/complex pair sequences. In even degree each equatorial circle bounds a real integral two-chain. Subtracting a complex normalization hemisphere, and then complex-conjugating, shows the corresponding torsion class equals the half degree modulo the global degree gcd; in particular all these classes generate the unique order-two subgroup. The real/complex boundary diagram identifies the full kernel by normalized-degree parity and the free quotient by the RP2 embedding character, giving the claimed exact sequence and index. Finite exact-arithmetic checker models (1290 cases) support, but do not replace, the all-degree proof. Risks: hinges on the integral chain orientation/conjugation identity and the graph exact sequence; both reconstructed in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The initiating Yoshinaga source supplies the graph framework, rational spanning, and an integral cokernel formula only when the global degree gcd is odd. The even case is excluded there. The new result computes the half-degree torsion image and the integral kernel and index for all even component degrees; the odd formula cannot imply these. Brown-Dupont uses Q or C coefficients, which lose the exact torsion index. Indexed mathematical-record searches and accessible primary full text did not establish equivalent coverage. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: Closes the parity boundary in a motivated integer-lattice problem left outside the odd-gcd case of the source. Gives a complete general kernel and sharp exact index, detects dependence on a real embedding character independent of complex Betti numbers, and distinguishes same-degree two-conic real forms (surjective versus index two). This is not a generic textbook deduction from knowing the complement torsion: the real chamber torsion-intersection requires the geometric conjugation lemma. No unproved downstream theorem is needed for this structural value.
